newsitem.title: FINLAND: Soft Helsinki ends off lows but on its toes.
newsitem.headline: Soft Helsinki ends off lows but on its toes.

text.p: Finnish shares ended clearly lower but a shade above session lows as the Dow industrials and bourse engine Nokia started higher in the U.S., but sentiment remained wary, brokers said.
Total losses were limited as many sellers were sidelined, waiting for for clues from the U.S. on whether the bull market is ending, but some money had started to go out of mutual funds.
"Some one-two percent has left funds, so there is some selling pressure from there," said one broker, but added that the day was characterised by fast-money operators.

The FOX derivatives and portfolio index fell 1.82 percent to 1,184.1 points and the HEX general index was down 1.70 perecnt at 3,451.3 points. Volume was a moderate 681 million markka with 39 percent in Nokia.
Brokers were waiting for signals from central bank meetings this week, and one said the dollar's moves were also in focus.
Another broker said the market could be turning sour although the U.S. showed signs of recovery.
"It takes more than a morning to make a baisse market; remember that most of the spring and early summer it was a hausse and we did not quite realise it," he said.
"Those who could have put their hand under this market today deliberately did not," he added.

Raisio, Nokia and Neste which have been driving gains this summer were now the biggest drags on the FOX index -- Raisio fell 20.00 markka or 3.6 percent to 535.00, Nokia was down 8.50 markka or 1.87 percent at 446.00 and Neste closed down 5.00 markka or 3.45 percent at 140.00 markka.
Fiskars bucked the trend on above-forecast H1 earnings.

It rose 15.00 markka or 3.1 percent to 505.00 after reporting first half profit after financial items at 219 markka, beating last year's total by one million markka and the highest forecast by 15 million.
It was one of only 12 advancing issues, while 86 declined and were unchanged.
Leading banking group Merita fell 0.20 markka or 0.87 percent to close at 22.90 in lively 44 million markka trade.
